newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to sell radio spectrum for mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Australia to sell radio spectrum for mobile phones.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday mobile phone services would be expanded and improved by its plan to sell more wireless band width.

Communications Minister Richard Alston said in a statement the government's decision to auction spectrum in the 800 MHz and 1800 MHz bands would benefit new entrants in Australia's deregulated telecommunications market.
The 800 MHz band is currently used for analogue mobile phone services and the 1800 MHz for fixed link communications, he said.
In the major capital cities the government would also provide 20 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 Mhz band, and 45 MHz in the 1800 MHz band.
Regional areas would receive 15 MHz of the paired spectrum in both bands.
Draft licence conditions would also be prepared in consultation with carriers, Alston said.

This would prevent established carriers Telstra Corp, Optus Communications Pty Ltd and Vodafone Group Plc from bidding for the first 10 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band in major capital cities, and five MHz of paired 800 MHz elsewhere, he said.
No individual would be able to buy more than 10 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, or more than 15 MHz in the 1800 MHz.

The government also planned to prepare draft licence conditions for limited analogue AMPS resale and reciprocal roaming rights between analogue AMPS service and the 800 MHZ digital mobile services, Alston said.
Analogue AMPS services will be phased out by 2000 following a review scheduled for 1999.
